431762229.source: Two fresh detector-sector difference stacks repeatedly favor TIC431762222; fixed neighbour/target residual SSE ratios are0.0090/0.0188. Free Gaussian deficits lie close to that neighbour. The ratios are descriptive, not calibrated probabilities.
431762229.geometry: The contaminating eclipse interval isapproximately1.94d; the original screen alias is rejected as a target eclipse period. No target Gaia orbit association is inferred.
431762229.limitations: The contaminant is an inferred EB host; its catalogue novelty and precision binary orbit were not independently adjudicated. Source model systematics remain.
431762229.next_check: Higher resolution eclipse photometry can verify the contaminating host.

9396327.assessment: Six fully covered primary events repeat in raw flux with depth28–29percent and consistent discrete morphology. Independent aperture reduction reproduces the events and the signed deficit favors the target. The Gaia-orbit geometry check remains unresolved.
9396327.source: Sector80 free Gaussian deficit lies0.56arcsec from target. Capable TIC neighbours51.4/55.9arcsec away have fixed neighbour/target SSE ratios74.9/70.5, strongly worse descriptively. The independent custom aperture reproduces repeated eclipses.
9396327.geometry: Representative six-event regression gives2.441670686d (timing residuals below0.00056d); Gaia2.441934355+/-0.000085226d. A sector-end partial event was excluded because its distorted timing shifts the inferred period. Approximate conjunction A offset0.347d versus propagated covariance0.116d; period differences alone do not veto an EB. Duration3.36h is feasible relative to central4.81h. Secondary-event phase and propagated orbital phase prevent claiming a fully consistent Gaia association.
9396327.limitations: Real on-target repeating EB; PROBABLE because the Gaia geometry/association check is unresolved. One fresh detector sector only; same-photon independent reduction. No firm by-catch flag: a modest period mismatch does not establish a separate orbit.
9396327.next_check: Refine Gaia conjunction predictions with orbital posterior and measure a second clean sector or obtain new RVs to test the orbit association.

183994341.assessment: Four repeated primary eclipses with raw depths25–29percent are on target and recovered independently. The eclipse period is approximately14.6655d; the ASAS-SN catalogue lists an incompatible2.9324d alias. The target is a known prior EB and excluded from new additions.
183994341.source: Sectors91/92 free Gaussian offsets1.71/1.58arcsec favor the target; closest capable neighbours38arcsec or farther give substantially worse fixed-source residuals (ratios22.8–44.1). Independent custom apertures reproduce repeated eclipses.
183994341.geometry: Four-event regression P14.665514216d versus Gaia14.670950076+/-0.003882078d. Approximate conjunction offset1.81d with propagated covariance0.93d and conservative absolute-sum1.76d; duration16.18h versus approximate central23.03h is physically feasible. The period, propagated approximate phase and duration are compatible with the Gaia orbit at current precision; the roughly1.9sigma phase difference alone is not a physical veto.
183994341.limitations: Real repeated on-target known EB. Approximate Gaia conjunction phase and radii limit characterization. Catalogue period conflict is retained rather than forcing catalogue cycles. No new-discovery claim.
183994341.next_check: Resolve ASAS-SN period alias and obtain RV/orbital posterior or a joint timing/geometry analysis to settle the Gaia association.
183994341.association: compatible at approximate current precision; phase uncertainty retained
